headline: Gut microbiome databases link microbial features to host disease across cohorts
label: Gut Microbiome Host Association
summary: Recent releases consolidate large human gut microbiome and gut disease datasets into reusable public resources.
synthesis: The dominant thread in this set is public resources that consolidate gut microbiome and gut disease data for reuse. GutBiomeDB integrates human gut microbiome samples at the scale of 168 464 samples, and gutDBase integrates transcriptomic and microbial data from 175 bulk and single-cell datasets across 15 gut-related diseases. What is new here is the joint organization of transcriptomic and microbial layers across multiple disease contexts within one resource, rather than a single shared analytical method. Other items in the set, including GPBench for genomic prediction, tModBase for tRNA modifications, and PmiREN3.0 for plant microRNAs, address different biological questions and do not share this gut-focused scope.
